captureRateCorrect_meta.keyed_by: English display name; wild (non-boss) form preferred where a name had boss/alpha variants
captureRateCorrect_meta.crosscheck: 407 codenames present in BOTH repos: 0 value mismatches (perfect agreement).
captureRateCorrect_meta.interpretation: Higher = EASIER to catch (multiplier on capture probability). Starters (Lamball/Chikipi/Cattiva)=1.5; most pals=1.0; a few hard pals <1.0 (Mimog 0.8).
captureRateCorrect_meta.notable_finding: All Legendaries (Jetragon/JetDragon, Frostallion/IceHorse, Necromus, Paladius, etc.) have CaptureRateCorrect = 1.0 in BOTH datamines. The oft-repeated '0.1 capture rate for legendaries' is NOT this field; their difficulty comes from high level + HP, not this multiplier.

spheres_meta.important: Palworld's CURRENT capture model does NOT use a flat per-sphere probability multiplier. Each sphere maps to a 'capture level' (CaptureSphereLevelMap) that is compared against the target Pal's level in CalcCaptureRate. The 'mult' values are legacy community estimates from the launch-era simplified model and are only approximate; the datamined truth is 'captureLevel_datamined'.

captureFormula: NOT datamined as a readable equation: the actual routine is BP_PalGameSetting_C::CalcCaptureRate, which is Unreal Engine Blueprint BYTECODE and is not decompiled in either repo (only the function stub/name is present). The DATAMINED CONSTANTS that feed it (all from BP_PalGameSetting.json) are: per-Pal CaptureRateCorrect (see above); sphere capture-level (Pal 7 / Mega 14 / Giga 20 / Hyper 27 / Ultra 33 / Legendary 38 / Ultimate 44 / Exotic 50 / Sol 58 / Ancient 64); status-ailment additive bonus CaptureRateAddByStatusMap = +0.3 each for Poison/Burn/Wetness/Freeze/Electrical/Muddy/IvyCling/Darkness and +0.35 for Sleep; leg-hold (grapple/partner-skill hold) additive bonus CaptureRateAdd_ByLegHold = +0.5; IgnoreFirstCaptureFailedHPRate = 0.5 (if the Pal's HP is above 50%, the very first sphere thrown is forced to break out); CaptureJudgeRateArray = [0.444444, 0.333333, 0.222222] (the three per-shake break-out check thresholds). COMMUNITY-DOCUMENTED FORM of the probability (labelled community-sourced, NOT verbatim from these repos): CaptureProbability = BaseRate x (1 - HPcurrent/HPmax) x SpherePower x CaptureRateCorrect x LevelFactor x (1 + StatusBonuses + LegHoldBonus + NightBonus + AlphaPenalty), then clamped to <=1.0 (100%). The three shakes are then each rolled against CaptureJudgeRateArray; success on all three (plus the >50% HP first-throw rule) yields a catch. Variables: BaseRate (community base constant, ~ handled inside CalcCaptureRate, not exposed); HPcurrent/HPmax = lower HP -> higher rate; SpherePower = derived from the sphere's capture level vs Pal level; CaptureRateCorrect = the per-Pal multiplier above; LevelFactor = higher Pal level lowers the rate; night/alpha modifiers and the exact BaseRate/level curve are NOT present in these two repos.

inheritance.countWeights_note: DATAMINED array Combi_PassiveInheritNum = [4,3,2,1] gives the CANDIDATE counts of passives inherited from the COMBINED parent pool. The array lists the possible values only; the per-count probability WEIGHTING is inside CalcCombi bytecode and is NOT in the data table. Community consensus treats the selection as roughly uniform among 1-4.
inheritance.randomTraitChance_note: No single scalar exists. DATAMINED array Combi_PassiveRandomAddNum = [4,3,2,1] gives the candidate counts of ADDITIONAL random passives added on top of inherited ones (total passives capped at 4). Which specific random passive is rolled is weighted by each passive skill's LotteryWeight field in DT_PassiveSkill_Main.json.
inheritance.notes: Child passive skills are drawn from the union of both parents' passives; the number taken is one of Combi_PassiveInheritNum=[4,3,2,1]; then additional random passives (count from Combi_PassiveRandomAddNum=[4,3,2,1]) may be added, capped at 4 total. Combi_TalentInheritNum=[3,2,1] governs IV/talent inheritance count (HP/Attack/Defense). Combi_BossPalRate=0.05 = 5% chance the bred child is an Alpha/boss variant. Passive count DISTRIBUTION/weights are datamined only as candidate arrays; exact per-count probabilities are in Blueprint bytecode (community estimates: uniform-ish among the candidates).
